# KANERVA: the dollar of Mexico

## What is the dollar of Mexico? (THE DOLLAR OF MEXICO, AND KANERVA'S OTHER EXAMPLES)

Two moves, the tie and the vote, are enough to ask this and get an answer. A country is a bundle of three ties. Tie two countries together and you get a map between them. Push **dollar** through the map and **peso** comes out. Each card shows one step on the first 40 of the 10,000 bits.

### King is to queen as man is to woman

This one is not in Kanerva’s paper. It is the classic word analogy, built here with the same two moves and roles we chose: KIND, RANK and SEX.

Source for cards 1 to 9: P. Kanerva, “What We Mean When We Say ‘What’s the Dollar of Mexico?’: Prototypes and Mapping in Concept Space”, AAAI Fall Symposium on Quantum Informatics for Cognitive, Social, and Semantic Processes, 2010 (Technical Report FS-10-08, pp. 2-6; the paper). The paper writes USTATES, MEXICO and SWEDEN with the roles NAM, CAP and MON; the cards spell them out. It also says what a word like this is for: “D can later be retrieved by addressing the memory with A or with a ‘noisy’ version of it that is similar to A. The address A is also called a memory cue.” On this site the word is **address**, and a damaged one is a **noisy address**.
